title: About
text:
About Me
I’m Naqiao Gu, a graduate student in Applied Business Analytics at Boston University.
My background is more business-focused than programming-focused, so one of my goals in AD688 is to understand how cloud tools and big data systems are actually used in business analytics.
For this course, I’m working with AWS EC2, Python, PySpark, GitHub, and Quarto. I prefer learning by setting things up myself, testing them, and fixing problems when something does not work.
Outside class, I’m especially interested in business analysis, operations, and data-driven decision making.

title: Naqiao’s Cloud Lab
text:
I’m a Business Analytics student at Boston University.
This site is for my AD688 course work. I’m using it to keep track of what I actually set up and test during the semester, including AWS EC2, Python, PySpark, Quarto, and GitHub.
I’m still getting used to the technical side of cloud analytics, so this site is basically a record of me building things step by step and making sure they actually work.


I set up PySpark on my AWS EC2 instance and used this small example to make sure the environment was working correctly.

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = (
    SparkSession.builder
    .master("local[2]")
    .appName("Naqiao AD688")
    .getOrCreate()
)

tools = [
    ("Python", "3.12"),
    ("PySpark", "4.0.4"),
    ("Quarto", "1.10")
]

df = spark.createDataFrame(tools, ["Tool", "Version"])
df.show()

spark.stop()
